test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Hari travels from City A to City B. If Hari drives his car at 1/4 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 39 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Hari would take to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Speed Ratio** (Normal : New) = 4 : 1

**Time Ratio** (Normal : New) = 1 : 4 (Since Time ∝ 1/Speed for constant distance)

Difference in time units = 4 − 1 = 3 units

Given difference = 39 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 39 ÷ 3 = 13 minutes

**Normal Time** (1 unit) = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05d8249cbc308d3a6123d13da5341c19971779385cc493a5f675745aa5a00e3e.png] 
**Given:**

Normal speed = S, New speed = S/4

Time difference (Δt) = 39 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let normal time be T. Then new time = T + 39

⇒ Since Distance is constant, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ S × T = (S/4) × (T + 39)

⇒ 4T = T + 39

⇒ 3T = 39

⇒ T = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the **distance** is constant, the time taken is inversely proportional to the speed (T ∝ 1/S). If speed becomes 1/n times, time becomes n times.

Late/Early Concept Formula

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × Difference in time. This is useful for finding the actual distance between two points.</p
